ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: 325
In a sample of 500 students from statistics courses in the fall semester, 312 earned a grade of C or higher. In the spring semester, 400 of the 525 students sampled earned a grade of C or higher. If we treat the fall semester as "sample 1" and the spring semester as "sample 2," what is the appropriate standardized test statistic to determine whether a smaller proportion of students passed in the fall?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a sample of 500 students from statistics courses in the fall semester, 312 earned a grade of C or higher. In the spring semester, 400 of the 525 students sampled earned a grade of C or higher. If we treat the fall semester as "sample 1" and the spring semester as "sample 2," what is the appropriate standardized test statistic to determine whether a smaller proportion of students passed in the fall?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The image shows the standardized statistic formula for the two-proportion z test: z = (p-hat_1 - p-hat_2) / sqrt[((X1+X2)/(n1+n2))(1 - (X1+X2)/(n1+n2))(1/n1 + 1/n2)]. The image also substitutes the values as numerator = 312/500 - 400/525, and denominator uses pooled proportion = (312+400)/(500+525). Then reason: fall is sample 1, so X1 = 312, n1 = 500; spring is sample 2, so X2 = 400, n2 = 525. p-hat_1 = 312/500 = 0.624, p-hat_2 = 400/525 ≈ 0.7619. The pooled proportion is (312+400)/(500+525) = 712/1025 ≈ 0.6946. Substitute into the formula: z = (0.624 - 0.7619) / sqrt[0.6946(1 - 0.6946)(1/500 + 1/525)] ≈ -4.792. Because what is being tested is whether fall is smaller, maintain the order of p-hat_1 - p-hat_2, so the statistic is negative.

method.method_draft: Set up the hypothesis test conceptually without needing to start from the visual formula. From the text, define the fall pass proportion as p1 and the spring pass proportion as p2, with observed sample proportions p-hat_1 = 312/500 = 0.624 and p-hat_2 = 400/525 ≈ 0.7619. For the null hypothesis p1 = p2, combine the samples to estimate the common pass rate: p-hat_pool = (312 + 400)/(500 + 525). The standard error under the null is sqrt[p-hat_pool(1 - p-hat_pool)(1/500 + 1/525)]. Then compute z = (0.624 - 0.7619)/SE. Since the alternative is that the fall proportion is smaller, the fall-minus-spring difference should be used, yielding z ≈ -4.792.
